learning_objective: 🎯 Unravel the journey of your clothes—from tiny fibers to spun yarn, and finally into the beautiful fabrics and apparel you wear!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A fiber is the smallest hair-like unit of a fabric. Fibers can be Natural (cotton from plants, wool/silk from animals) or Man-made/Synthetic (nylon, polyester, rayon, which are made from chemicals).
Fibers are too weak to be woven into cloth on their own. They are twisted together in a process called 'Spinning' to create a long, strong, continuous thread known as Yarn.

Yarns are turned into fabrics mostly through two methods: Weaving (interlacing two sets of yarns on a loom, like a grid) and Knitting (interlocking loops of a single yarn, which makes the fabric stretchy, like a sweater).
The clothes we choose depend on the climate, occasion, age, and comfort. For example, cotton is preferred in summer because it absorbs sweat, while synthetic clothes are avoided near fire.
When fabric comes off the loom, it looks dull. 'Finishing' involves treatments like bleaching, dyeing, printing, or making it water-resistant to improve its appearance and usefulness.

fun_activity.title: 🔍 The Wardrobe Detective
fun_activity.instructions: Go to your closet and check the tags on three different shirts. Find one that is 100% Cotton (natural) and one that is Polyester (synthetic). Feel the difference in texture and stretch!

exam_tips: 📌 Differentiate clearly between Natural Fibers (cotton, silk) and Synthetic Fibers (nylon, polyester).
📌 Know the difference between Weaving (uses two sets of yarn, warp and weft) and Knitting (uses loops of a single yarn).
📌 'Spinning' is the process of converting fibers into yarn.
quick_recap: ⭐ The sequence of clothing is: Fiber -> Yarn -> Fabric -> Apparel.
⭐ Silk is an animal fiber obtained from the cocoon of the silkworm.
⭐ Finishes make fabrics more durable, beautiful, and functional.
